name: The Secrets Gate Catches Planted Material
greenMarker: objects to planted material and stays quiet without it
note: 0-4 checks the repository; this checks 0-4. It was added after a reproduction showed that 0-4 read staged file NAMES but never staged CONTENT: with a credential in the index and the working copy edited clean, 0-4 printed 'Repository Clean' and exited 0. Git counts the index as a reachability root, so the `git fsck --unreachable` step could not cover it either — a staged blob is reachable by definition. The mutations below break the index scan and the control separately, because a bait test that fires on everything proves nothing and a bait test that fires on nothing proves less.

mutations.name: the index scan is removed and only the working tree is read
mutations.why: This restores the exact shipped gap. `git grep` with no revision reads the working tree; --cached reads what is queued for the next commit. Dropping the flag makes the index scan a second working-tree scan, so case C goes green again while a credential sits staged. If this survives, case C is decorative.

mutations.name: the gate objects to a repository with nothing wrong
mutations.why: The control, broken on purpose. A gate that fails on everything catches every bait, and its greens would then carry no information at all. Case A has to notice. Adding a pattern that matches ordinary text is the cheapest way a real change could cause this — a broadened regex, a dropped exclusion.
mutations.replace:
{ name: 'private key block', re: /-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/ },
  { name: 'qa control', re: /throwaway/ },
mutations.expectFailure: must pass, or nothing below means anything

mutations.name: the history scan stops reading merge commits
mutations.why: Added 2026-09-30 with the single-pass history scan. A credential added inside a merge commit exists only as that merge's diff, which git log -p prints only with -m. Case E plants exactly that.

mutations.name: the history path list reads only the current tree
mutations.why: The path check over history is now one git log instead of one ls-tree per commit. Reading only what is checked out now would miss a keystore that was committed and deleted — case F. (First written as git log -1, which SURVIVED correctly: the deleting commit still names the deleted file.)
